newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols steady ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols steady ahead of jobs data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were mostly steady in late trade ahead of Friday's August U.S. employment report, dealers said.
Volatilities had pipped up slightly early in the day as underlying markets tumbled on news of a drop in weekly jobless claims. But they soon recoiled as the market pared losses.
"They're really just taking out theta (time decay)," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatilities for October and December T-bond futures options stood at around 11.8 and 10.5 percent respectively, virtually unchanged from late Wednesday levels.
The upward pressure on volatilities ahead of the numbers was partly mitigated by time decay as premiums had started the week at relatively rich levels, traders said.
Still, as usual before key economic figures, shorter-dated out-of-the-money options saw some good buying.
Traders noted call buying at strike prices of 108 and 109 in batches of 500 to 1,000 lots.
On the other hand, a bank was said to have sold 2,500 contracts of December 112 calls. Several large put sales were also reported.

Among other major trades, one house was said to have bought 2,000 legs of October 104/105 put spreads while selling 2,000 legs of 109/111 call spreads in a package. A European firm was seen buying 5,000 lots of December 112 calls and selling 1,000 of December 106 puts, covered against futures.
Analysts said that although the bond market's outlook was bearish overall after damaging declines in recent weeks, people could be taken by surprise if the jobs figures were weak.
"This is the first time that, going into these numbers, the technical picture on a short-term basis is so negative," said Terence Gabriel, a technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc.

According to a Reuters poll, economists have forecast on average an increase of 244,000 in August non-farm payrolls against a rise of 193,000 in July. The jobless rate was seen falling to 5.3 percent in August from 5.4 a month earlier.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, volatilities for December and March eurodollar futures options stood at 14.3 and 13.1 percent, a touch higher than Wednesday's closes.
A brokerage trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said volume was moderate but there appeared to be little directional bias. -Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
